item.title: Coupled responses of aboveground and belowground net primary productivity stability to nitrogen deposition in grasslands
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04163-x

Nitrogen deposition synchronously reduces above- and belowground plant productivity stability via an allocation trade-off between mean productivity and variability, with stronger declines under longer or more intensive treatments, based on a meta-analysis.
item.dc:title: Coupled responses of aboveground and belowground net primary productivity stability to nitrogen deposition in grasslands
item.dc:creator: Yaodan Zhang
Siyuan Gao
Xinxin Wang
Huiying Liu

item.title: Drying and rewetting of riverbed sediments results in cold to neutral biogeochemical moments
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04081-y

Drying and rewetting sediments caused near-neutral or extreme cold moments with suppressed oxygen consumption in perennial and non-perennial streams, with no meaningful hot moments observed, based on wet/dry experiments with sediments from 64 streams across the Continental United States.
item.dc:title: Drying and rewetting of riverbed sediments results in cold to neutral biogeochemical moments

item.title: Microbially mediated interactions between enhanced weathering and carbon inputs shift soil organic carbon dynamics
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04143-1

When labile carbon is available, enhanced weathering can increase soil carbon storage mainly through microbial processing rather than by creating new mineral surfaces for carbon binding, based on a 55-week soil microcosm experiment with olivine amendments.
item.dc:title: Microbially mediated interactions between enhanced weathering and carbon inputs shift soil organic carbon dynamics

item.title: Low-carbon technologies support energy security by buffering energy price shocks
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04131-5

Energy supply crises matter because their economic impacts extend beyond energy markets. This Comment argues that energy security should be understood by how energy systems transmit price shocks to the wider economy. Low-carbon technologies matter because, unlike fossil fuels, they dampen this transmission through the economy.
item.dc:title: Low-carbon technologies support energy security by buffering energy price shocks
item.dc:creator: Jose A. Ordonez
Matthias Weitzel
Camille Van Der Vorst
Rafael Garaffa

item.title: Persistent seasonal deoxygenation alters benthic metabolic processes and accelerates hypoxia feedbacks in the Baltic Sea
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04120-8

Persistent seasonal oxygen depletion weakens sediment resilience and increases sulfide release risk, as shown by a 15-month SW Baltic Sea study integrating water column monitoring, sediment geochemistry, metabolic rates, omics analyses, and historical comparisons
item.dc:title: Persistent seasonal deoxygenation alters benthic metabolic processes and accelerates hypoxia feedbacks in the Baltic Sea
